results.title: LLM Engine Scope Validation
results.headline: Complete scope generates a draft; incomplete scope stops before a model call.
results.success_criteria: Complete scope produces a schema-valid draft; incomplete scope returns needs_input before model generation.
results.methodology: Run one complete assignment and one incomplete RFQ fixture through the engine.
results.explanation: The engine refuses to spend a model call when the assignment is missing required scope, so incomplete requests stop safely and cheaply.
results.technical_explanation: Pydantic validates the Assignment contract, then the scope gate runs before retrieval/model generation. needs_input is a typed result, not an exception.

complete_assignment.problem: Create a preliminary improvement plan for a fictional city department whose intake process is inconsistent and slow.
complete_assignment.intended_result: Provide a reviewable draft plan that improves intake consistency and turnaround time.
constraints: Use only the synthetic fixture evidence

incomplete_assignment.problem: List the qualifications a consulting firm should have.

results.title: Retrieval Relevance
results.execution_phase: Status Update 2 — Data Ingestion & Retrieval Baseline
results.headline: The labeled retrieval set meets the top-5 relevance target and blocks forbidden evidence.
results.success_criteria: At least 80% of answerable labeled queries return the expected evidence in the top five; forbidden evidence never enters model context.
results.methodology: Run a 12-query labeled retrieval baseline against approved and forbidden evidence.
results.explanation: Retrieval quality is measured before generation because even a strong model cannot produce a trustworthy report from the wrong or forbidden evidence.
results.technical_explanation: The demo ranks evidence by deterministic token overlap, filters external_model_allowed=false first, and evaluates expected top-five behavior.

results.title: Structured Report Generation
results.execution_phase: Status Update 3 — First Integrated Consulting Report
results.headline: The engine produces a schema-valid draft containing every requested consulting section.
results.success_criteria: Every requested section appears, or an explicit information gap is returned; historical values are labeled.
results.methodology: Generate a consulting report requesting findings, alternatives, recommendation, implementation steps, and risks.
results.explanation: This is where retrieved evidence becomes a structured consulting deliverable instead of free-form chatbot text.
results.technical_explanation: Week 4's hardened engine validates the provider response against the Report schema and required-section list before accepting it.

results.title: Citation Traceability
results.execution_phase: Status Update 3 — First Integrated Consulting Report
results.headline: Every accepted citation resolves to retrieved evidence, and a fake citation is rejected.
results.success_criteria: Every accepted citation resolves to retrieved evidence; a made-up evidence ID is rejected.
results.methodology: Validate a normal report, then replace one citation with a nonexistent chunk ID.
results.explanation: Valid citation IDs resolve to retrieved evidence, while a made-up citation is rejected before the report can be accepted.
results.technical_explanation: Citation IDs are mapped to evidence_chunk_id values and checked against the exact set of chunks provided to the model.

results.title: Prompt Injection / Unsupported Evidence
results.execution_phase: Status Update 4 — Security, Revision & Failure Handling
results.headline: Instructions hidden inside source text cannot change permissions, and unsupported exact numbers are rejected.
results.success_criteria: Source-document instructions cannot alter permissions/rules; unsupported exact claims are rejected.
results.methodology: Feed prompt-injection text and a separate unsupported numeric claim through the hardened engine.
results.explanation: Retrieved documents are treated as untrusted data, so text inside a document cannot override the engine rules or permissions.
results.technical_explanation: The engine flags known injection patterns, forces an instruction boundary, and performs deterministic exact-number support checks against cited evidence.

results.title: Model Failure Recovery
results.execution_phase: Status Update 4 — Security, Revision & Failure Handling
results.headline: Timeouts retry only within the configured bound, and malformed output fails without creating a report.
results.success_criteria: Timeout/provider failure returns a controlled typed error with bounded attempts and no false completed report.
results.methodology: Force provider timeout and malformed JSON behaviors through the mock provider.
results.explanation: Provider failure is treated as a normal system state: the engine returns a clear error instead of pretending a completed report exists.
results.technical_explanation: EnginePolicy caps attempts/output size. Provider timeout and malformed JSON are converted to typed failures and report remains null.

malformed_output.message: Provider returned malformed JSON: Expecting ',' delimiter

results.title: LLM Evidence Quality
results.headline: The accepted report meets the evidence-support target with no critical unsupported claims.
results.success_criteria: At least 90% factual support, 100% requested-section coverage, and zero critical unsupported claims.
results.methodology: Score the accepted report with the Week 5 repeatable quality rubric.
results.explanation: Quality is measured with a repeatable rubric instead of relying on a subjective statement that one report simply looks better.
results.technical_explanation: score_result combines deterministic support/citation/coverage checks with explicitly labeled reviewer scores.

results.title: Report Usefulness
results.headline: The reviewer rubric requires at least 4/5 for accuracy, completeness, usefulness, and feasibility.
results.success_criteria: Reviewer scores accuracy, completeness, usefulness, and feasibility at least 4/5 each.
results.methodology: Enter or accept reviewer scores in the GUI and validate all four dimensions.
results.explanation: The reviewer gate is intentionally interactive: any score below 4/5 fails the usefulness check, while restoring all dimensions to 4/5 or higher passes it.
results.technical_explanation: This checkpoint is intentionally human-in-the-loop: usefulness and feasibility cannot be established only by schema/citation checks.

results.title: API Cost Control
results.headline: The engine reserves cost before a provider call; an over-budget run makes zero paid calls and normal usage is reconciled.
results.success_criteria: A request exceeding its configured allowance produces zero provider calls; normal usage is still cost-accounted.
results.methodology: Run the tiny-budget fixture and a normal deterministic usage calculation.
results.explanation: The budget guard runs before provider use, so an over-budget request is blocked with provider_calls = 0 before money can be spent.
results.technical_explanation: BudgetLedger reserves a conservative maximum atomically before provider use and reconciles the observed usage afterward.

results.title: Release Compatibility — Engine Portion
results.plan_owner: Full Team / Yasha lead; Jai engine portion
results.headline: The engine release freezes its selected configuration and preserves the shared Assignment/Report contracts.
results.success_criteria: The frozen engine configuration and shared Assignment/Report contracts remain versioned and compatible.
results.methodology: Load the frozen Week 5 comparison and inspect the shared contract schemas and version labels.
results.explanation: The accepted release is frozen so later testing uses the same prompt, retrieval settings, model choice, and shared data contracts.
results.technical_explanation: The acceptance check verifies shared identifiers in the Pydantic schemas plus frozen prompt/retrieval/corpus version metadata.

results.title: Full System Demonstration — Engine Portion
results.headline: One end-to-end run now finishes with the same structured report information that the application layer can render for the City user.
results.success_criteria: A prepared assignment proceeds through retrieval, report generation, evidence-quality validation, and cost accounting.
results.methodology: Execute the complete controlled consulting-engine path and return the final structured report plus metrics.
results.explanation: This is the complete engine path: problem in, approved evidence selected, structured report generated, then validated before the application displays it.
results.technical_explanation: This composition reuses the same acceptance functions instead of inventing a separate demo-only path.

results.title: Controlled System Failure Demo — Engine Portion
results.headline: A controlled model outage returns a visible typed failure without creating a duplicate report or destroying the prior report.
results.success_criteria: Model unavailability produces a visible controlled failure without a duplicate report; the prior successful report remains available.
results.methodology: Generate one successful report, then force a provider timeout on the next attempt.
results.explanation: The failed run returns report=null while the previously successful report remains available, preventing duplicate or misleading output.
results.technical_explanation: A failed provider call returns a typed error object and cannot overwrite the already accepted report object in the demonstration state.

results.title: Automatic Model Longevity
results.headline: The bonus longevity layer detects outdated models and requires benchmark approval before a replacement is proposed.
results.success_criteria: Outdated models are detected, approved replacements are benchmark-gated, and previous model IDs remain available for rollback.
results.methodology: Run the deterministic model lifecycle testbench already added to the repository.
results.explanation: The model registry lets future teams replace retired models through configuration and benchmark approval instead of rewriting the engine.
results.technical_explanation: The model registry separates provider model IDs from engine logic and requires a passed benchmark before a proposed registry migration.
